note: Outreach Pack wording and plan. The plan is the same 14-day touch plan as the Warm Desk tab in Citadel (tests/fixtures/outreach-plan.json must match). Fields in {braces} are filled from your list; any that cannot be filled keep the braces and the row is marked not ready. Every email ends with your name, your postal address and an easy way to say no. Nothing here sends anything: you load the file into your own Gmail merge or sending tool and press start yourself.

review.subject: Noticed this on your Google page
review.body:
{hi}

I was looking at {business} on Google and noticed {gap_line}. There is a clear gap between you and {competitor}, and I found a simple way to close it. I recorded a quick 2-minute video walking through what I mean. Would it be okay if I sent it over?

review.subject: What that gap may be costing {business}
review.body:
{hi}

Following up on my note. When people search for {service} in {city}, they tend to choose from the businesses with the most recent reviews, so a gap like {gap_line} can send some of them to someone else. I can show you the numbers from your own page in two minutes. Shall I send the video?

review.subject: What it looks like once this is fixed
review.body:
{hi}

A short picture of the fix: after each finished job your customer gets a friendly message with a direct link to review you on Google, and you watch the number move. I have a demo of it (labelled DEMO, not a client) I can send. Would 15 minutes this week be worth it?

review.subject: Should I close your file?
review.body:
{hi}

I have written a couple of times about the reviews on {business}'s Google page. If the timing is wrong or it is not a priority, that is completely fine, and I will not write again. If it is worth 15 minutes, reply with "yes" and I will send two times that suit you.

inquiry.subject: I sent your website a question
What happens after someone fills in your form
inquiry.body:
{hi}

Following up on my note about the form on {business}'s site. Here is the flow I would set up, shown in a demo (labelled DEMO, not a client): someone fills in the form, they get an answer within about a minute, a few questions find out if it is a good fit, good-fit people pick a time on your calendar, and everyone else gets a follow-up until they are ready. You get one short report a month. Would 15 minutes this week be worth it so I can show you on your own form?
